indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer or counterparty has previous drug-related convictions or open-source reporting indicates connections to clandestine lab operations.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty with drug-conviction history or adverse-media link to clandestine lab
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer or counterparty is a chemical or pharmaceutical company in the PRC, Hong Kong, or another jurisdiction with a residential address or a business address shared with other similar businesses or that has no physical presence or shows other indicators of possible illicit shell company activity.
indicators.red_flag: PRC/HK chemical-pharma counterparty with shared/residential/no-physical address (shell indicators)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag an entity exhibiting shell or front-company markers â opaque or circular beneficial ownership, shared registered addresses or directors, recent incorporation with no observable operations â escalating when nominees or addresses recur across a cluster of related entities.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph
build_logic.source: corporate registry + KYC beneficial-ownership records + entity-resolution graph
build_logic.route: Tier-2 network alert â AML investigations gate

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A counterparty, with no supposed affiliation with the PRC, uses a PRC-based phone number or Internet Protocol (IP) address that is affiliated with the website of a Chinese chemical or pharmaceutical company.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty contact/IP resolves to PRC chemical-pharma site despite no stated PRC tie
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D10.

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer or counterparty is a vendor on an e-commerce or Darknet marketplace that advertises the sale of precursor chemicals (using chemical names, abbreviations, or CAS numbers in the advertisement) and manufacturing equipment used for the synthesis of illicit fentanyl and other synthetic opioids.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty advertises precursor-chemical / pill-press sales on e-commerce or Darknet marketplace
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer is a Mexican company that, according to open-source and commercially available reporting, is importing shipments of fentanyl precursor chemicals and manufacturing equipment without appropriate importing licenses and registrations in Mexico.
indicators.red_flag: Mexican importer moving precursor chemicals without required import licenses (OSINT-flagged)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D13 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence intelligence), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag trade or parcel-movement activity whose shipping routes, volumes, or fragmentation are inconsistent with the customer's business profile, escalating when logistics evidence does not reconcile with the associated payment flows or consignee relationships.
build_logic.window: rolling 60 days vs business profile baseline
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â trade-finance AML review gate

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer is a Mexican company with little or no online presence and is involved in the import of the same precursor chemicals and manufacturing equipment used in the synthesis of fentanyl.
indicators.red_flag: Precursor-importing Mexican company with little/no web presence
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: Multiple, seemingly unrelated Mexican importing companies share phone numbers, email addresses, or physical addresses and transact with the same PRC-based chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical companies.
indicators.red_flag: Unrelated Mexican importers sharing identifiers, funneling to one PRC chemical supplier
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D10 (Customer & account reference / entity-resolution data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Customer and Counterparty Profile Red Flags
indicators.flag: A customer is a Mexican importing company that predominantly transacts only with chemical or pharmaceutical companies in the PRC or Hong Kong for no apparent legitimate reason as compared to similar importers that transact with foreign chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical suppliers in multiple jurisdictions.
indicators.red_flag: Mexican importer transacting near-exclusively with PRC/HK chemical-pharma (peer-corridor anomaly)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D17 (Geographic / jurisdiction risk reference), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A customer sends low-dollar or virtual currency payments for no apparent legitimate purpose to beneficiaries involved in the chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries in the PRC, Hong Kong, or another jurisdiction.
indicators.red_flag: Low-dollar / virtual-currency payments to PRC/HK chemical-pharma beneficiaries
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Multiple customers send funds for no apparent legitimate purpose to the same beneficiary involved in the chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries in the PRC, Hong Kong, or another jurisdiction (i.e., many-to-one).
indicators.red_flag: Many-to-one funnel-in to a single PRC/HK chemical-pharma beneficiary
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.flag: A Mexico-based entity from an unrelated industry transacts with a PRC-based chemical or pharmaceutical company.  Alternatively, a PRC-based entity from an unrelated industry transacts with a Mexico-based chemical or pharmaceutical company.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-industry Mexico/PRC entity transacting with foreign chemical-pharma firm
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account whose inflow volume or wealth velocity is inconsistent with the customer's declared income, occupation, or stated source of funds, escalating when large credits lack a plausible origin for the customer's profile.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared income profile
build_logic.source: personal deposit ledger joined to onboarding income/occupation KYC data
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A customer engages in behavior that suggests efforts to evade the Currency Transaction Report (CTR) filing requirement (e.g., the customer alters or cancels a transaction when advised a CTR would be filed or engages in structuring with multiple cash transactions for under $10,000), as well as avoiding recordkeeping requirements.
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C4 (Structuring / sub-threshold & reporting-trigger evasion).

indicators.flag: A customer sends virtual currency payments to an address that is linked through blockchain analytics to beneficiaries associated with the PRC-based chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries or to individuals or entities listed in DOJ indictments and OFAC designations.
indicators.red_flag: Virtual-currency payments to address chain-linked to PRC chemical-pharma or OFAC/DOJ-listed entities
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer is a Mexican company that does not appear to be involved in the chemical manufacturing and pharmaceutical industries despite transactional activity indicating the procurement of fentanyl precursor chemicals and associated manufacturing equipment.
indicators.red_flag: Mexican company outside chemical-pharma sector with precursor-procurement transaction pattern
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared income profile
build_logic.source: personal deposit ledger joined to onboarding income/occupation KYC data
